outcome: Admission to special care nursery or neonatal intensive care unit (SCN/NICU)
Longer antenatal stay in hospital (>=2 days)
cohort: The study included 24,161 women who had a singleton birth in the Australian Capital Territory between 2009 and 2015, with available maternal weight and height information.
finding: Maternal overweight and obesity significantly contribute to a large proportion of obstetric complications and adverse pregnancy outcomes in the Australian Capital Territory.
mod_finding: Maternal overweight and obesity were associated with an increased risk of caesarean delivery, accounting for an estimated 15.5% of such deliveries.
cross-section timing: Data for births occurring between 2009-2015 were analysed.
